claims.text: FeCoNiCrAl bond coats deposited from 15–45 μm feedstock using conventional plasma-spray parameters exhibit a coating-thickness shortfall.
Increasing stand-off distance by 10–15%, reducing torch power by about 10%, and adding an in-flight Ar quench will increase deposition efficiency.
The combined intervention will produce a thicker coating than the conventional-process baseline.
The combined intervention will preserve coating integrity relative to the baseline.
The combined intervention will maintain minimal as-sprayed oxidation relative to the baseline.
The adjusted spray conditions produce slightly lower in-flight particle temperatures.
The adjusted spray conditions produce slightly lower in-flight particle velocities.
Slightly lower particle temperatures and velocities increase deposition yield by improving splat formation and impact bonding.
Increasing the stand-off distance gives particles additional time to decelerate.
The additional deceleration associated with increased stand-off distance optimizes particle flattening and adhesion on impact.
A moderate reduction in torch power prevents excessive particle heating.
Preventing excessive particle heating through reduced torch power decreases in-flight oxidation.
An in-flight Ar quench rapidly lowers particle temperature before substrate contact.
Ar-quench cooling limits oxidation while retaining enough particle kinetic energy for effective splat formation.
The intervention remains effective during deposition in a controlled inert atmosphere with substrates at ambient to moderately elevated temperatures.
The resulting coating will exhibit low oxide inclusion or low oxide-phase levels.
Excessive stand-off distance or excessive torch-power reduction can lower particle momentum below that required for adequate splat formation.
Particle momentum below the splat-formation threshold compromises deposit integrity.
